title: DatCol
text:
Reproducibility
All analyses are provided as individual Quarto (.qmd) notebooks, which can be rendered independently. Each notebook reads processed .rds files from the dataframes/ folder and generates publication-quality figures and statistical outputs (Table S2).
To reproduce the analyses:

Clone or download this repository to your local machine.
Install required R packages listed in R Session Info using renv or manually.
Render the notebooks using Quarto to generate figures and results.

All input data (dataframes/ and Tn-Seq/) is included in the repository. The notebooks read it through the BOX_PATH environment variable, which the .Renviron file at the repository root already sets to the repository folder (BOX_PATH="."), so no setup is needed. If you keep the data elsewhere, change that line to point to the folder that contains dataframes/ and Tn-Seq/, and restart R.
The whole project can be rendered using RStudio’s “Render” or “Build” options or in the terminal via:

quarto render

title: Tn-Seq Pipeline
text:
Reference genome and TA sites
We used Staphylococcus aureus subsp. aureus USA300_FPR3757 GCF_000013465.1 as reference genome. The assembly was downloaded from NCBI on 12/21/23. Curated versions of the assembly were manually created containing only the main chromosome NC_007793.1 (the 3 plasmids were removed) and saved as Sau_USA300_FPR3757.fasta and Sau_USA300_FPR3757.gff in data/TnSeq/RefSeqs.

gff_pfx = "Sau_USA300_FPR3757"
gff_dir = file.path(TnSeq_folder, "RefSeqs/Sau_USA300_FPR3757.gff")
genome_dir <- file.path(TnSeq_folder,"RefSeqs/Sau_USA300_FPR3757.fasta")

Sau_USA300_FPR3757.fasta was indexed for use with bowtie2 later in the pipeline

#conda activate Tn-Seq
bowtie2-build data/TnSeq/RefSeqs/Sau_USA300_FPR3757.fasta data/TnSeq/RefSeqs/USA300

For Mariner transposons, which only insert in TA sites, it is beneficial to identify all of the TA sites and restrict to these sites for downstream analysis. To generate a .csv file of all of the TA sites in a genome, the following code was used:

genome <- readDNAStringSet(genome_dir)
ta_sites <- vmatchPattern("TA", genome)
ta_vect <- unname(unlist(start(ta_sites)))
ta_df <- data_frame(sites = ta_vect)
write.csv(ta_df$sites, file.path(TnSeq_folder, "RefSeqs/Sau_USA300_FPR3757_TAsites.csv"))

title: Tn-Seq Pipeline
text:
Tn-seq Mapping
This section is based in the TnSeq2.sh script. This section processes the raw fastq files, maps the reads to the reference genome, and tallies the mapping results to identify insertion sites and read counts per site.

myPath="data/TnSeq/"

mkdir -p $myPath/logs
mkdir -p $myPath/bam
mkdir -p $myPath/sites
mkdir -p $myPath/genes

for file in $myPath/fastq/*.fastq.gz; do
    PREFIX=`basename ${file%.*.*}`
    echo "Initializing TnSeq analysis on $PREFIX"
    echo "TnSeq processing stats for $PREFIX" > $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    echo "Number of raw reads: " >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    zcat $file | grep -c '^@' >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
done


Trimming of IRs & Adaptors
This code chunk removes adapters by removing every sequence before the IR sequence using cutadapt (Martin, 2011). The number of reads post-trimming is logged for each sample. The -m 20 option ensures that only reads of at least 20 bp after trimming are retained, which helps to filter out very short reads that may not be informative for mapping.

myPath="data/TnSeq/"

#conda activate Tn-Seq
IR="GCCAACCTGTTA"

for file in $myPath/fastq/*.fastq.gz; do
    PREFIX=`basename ${file%.*.*}`
    echo "$PREFIX: Removing primer and IR sequences..."
    cutadapt -g $IR -m 20 --discard-untrimmed -o $myPath/fastq/$PREFIX.trim.fastq $file > $myPath/logs/$PREFIX.cutadapt_log.txt
    echo "Number of post-trimmed reads: " >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    grep -c '^@' $myPath/fastq/$PREFIX.trim.fastq >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
done

Some of the samples were resequenced, so we had to concatenate the trim files for the original and resequenced samples before moving forward with the analysis.

myPath="data/TnSeq/"

cd $myPath/fastq
cat 5772_021_S19_R1_001.trim.fastq 5772_021reseq_S1_R1_001.trim.fastq > 5772_021_S01_R1_001.trim.fastq
cat 5772_022_S20_R1_001.trim.fastq 5772_022reseq_S2_R1_001.trim.fastq > 5772_022_S00_R1_001.trim.fastq
cat 5772_027_S1_R1_001.trim.fastq 5772_027_S61_R1_001.trim.fastq > 5772_027_S00_R1_001.trim.fastq



Mapping to reference genome
This code chunk maps the reads to the reference genome using Bowtie2 (Langmead and Salzberg, 2012; Langmead et al., 2018) and processes the resulting SAM files with samtools (Danecek et al., 2021) to generate sorted BAM files containing only mapped, primary alignments. The mapping report from Bowtie2 and the number of mapped reads are logged for each sample.

myPath="data/TnSeq/"
GENOME=$myPath"RefSeqs/USA300"

#conda activate Tn-Seq

for file in $myPath/fastq/*.trim.fastq; do
    PREFIX=`basename ${file%.*.*}`
    echo "$PREFIX: Mapping with Bowtie2..."
    echo "Bowtie2 report:" >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    bowtie2 --end-to-end -p 16 -a -x $GENOME -U $myPath/fastq/$PREFIX.trim.fastq 2>> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt | \
    samtools view -b -F 4 -F 2048 | samtools sort -@ 16 -o $myPath/bam/$PREFIX-mapped.bam
    echo "Number of mapped reads:" >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    samtools view -c $myPath/bam/$PREFIX-mapped.bam >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
done



Tallying mapping results
This code chunk processes the mapped BAM files to identify unique insertion sites and count the number of reads mapping to each site. The results are saved in text files for each sample, and summary statistics about the number of insertion sites and the most frequent sites are logged.

myPath="data/TnSeq/"

#conda activate Tn-Seq

for file in $myPath/fastq/*.trim.fastq; do
    PREFIX=`basename ${file%.*.*}`
    echo "$PREFIX: Tallying mapping results..."
    samtools view -F 256 $myPath/bam/$PREFIX-mapped.bam | \
        awk '{if(($2) != 16) print $4; else print $4+length($10)}' | \
        sort | uniq -c | sort -k1nr \
        > $myPath/sites/$PREFIX-sites.txt
    echo "Number of insertion sites identified:" >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    wc -l $myPath/sites/$PREFIX-sites.txt >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    echo "Most frequent sites:" >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
    head -10 $myPath/sites/$PREFIX-sites.txt >> $myPath/logs/$PREFIX-TnSeq.txt
done

title: Tn-Seq Pipeline
text:
Essential Gene Analysis
This section is based on the Essential Gene Analysis script. The code in this section reads in the site counts generated in the previous section, generates expected datasets with the same number of sites and reads, bins the sites into genes using the TnGeneBin.pl script, and performs DESeq2 analysis to identify essential genes.

Counting reads per site and generating expected datasets
We manually made subfolders to separates the sites files for each sample type (input and lac) so that we could run the following code separately for each sample type. The code chunk below is where you select which sample type to run the analysis on. You will need to update the ctrl_pfx variable based on the sample type you are running (e.g. “input” or “lac”) as this is used in the naming of output files and summary stats.

# Run this code chunk separately for each sample type, updating the mydata and ctrl_pfx variables accordingly
mydata <- file.path(TnSeq_folder, "sites/sites_input")
ctrl_pfx = paste(gff_pfx, "input", sep = "_") #update name based on sample type

#mydata <- file.path(TnSeq_folder, "sites/sites_lac")
#ctrl_pfx = paste(gff_pfx, "lac", sep = "_") #update name based on sample type

This code chunk reads in the site counts for each sample, generates expected datasets with the same number of sites and reads, and outputs the read counts per site and gene boundaries for the binning script. It also outputs summary statistics about the number of sites and reads to a text file.

filenames <- dir(mydata, pattern = ".*-sites.txt", full.names = TRUE)
conditions <- sub("-sites.txt", "", filenames)

ctrl_reps = length(filenames)
num_expected = 100
out_pfx = paste(ctrl_pfx, "EssentialGenes_100", sep = "_")
to_trim = 0

# create summary stats file to record summary info

write(out_pfx, file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""))
write(paste( "\n", "input files:", sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
write(filenames, file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
write(paste( "\n", "gff: ", gff_pfx, sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
write(paste("\n", "to trim: ", to_trim, sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
write(paste("number of expected datasets: ", num_expected, sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)

# Read in sites files
        sites <- data.frame(Pos = c(0)) 
        for (i in 1:length(conditions)) {
                newsites <- read.table(paste(paste(conditions[i], sep = "/"), "sites.txt", sep = "-")) 
                colnames(newsites) <- c(paste("V", i, sep = ""), "Pos")
                newsites <- arrange(newsites,Pos)
                sites <- merge(sites, newsites, all = T) 
        }
        sites <- tail(sites, n = -1)
        sites[is.na(sites)] <- 0

        #output number of total and shared sites across samples. Need to edit based on number of samples.
        sites_total <- sites %>% mutate(numreps = (V1 > 0) + (V2 > 0)) %>% filter(numreps >= 1)
        write(paste("number of sites:", nrow(sites_total)), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        sites_shared <- sites %>% mutate(numreps = (V1 > 0) + (V2 > 0)) %>% filter(numreps >= 2)
        write(paste("number of sites shared by all samples:", nrow(sites_shared)), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)

        # Normalize data by reads/site
        colData <- data.frame(c(rep(ctrl_pfx, ctrl_reps)), condition = rep("treated", ctrl_reps))
        sitescds <- sites[,2:length(sites)] %>% round %>% DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(colData = colData, design = ~ 1)
        sitescds <- estimateSizeFactors(sitescds)
        #Output the normalized counts
        counts.norm <- counts(sitescds, normalized = F)
        rownames(counts.norm) <- sites$Pos

        # Initialize the list of genes, determine genome length
        #can add column names if your gff has extra columns
        gff <- read.delim(gff_dir, sep = "\t", fill = TRUE, skip = 9, header = FALSE, col.names = c("seqname", "source", "feature", "start", "end", "score", "strand", "frame", "att"))
        #change this value if your gff file contains anything besides genes that you want to read in
        gff <- gff[(gff$feature == "gene"),]

        # Initialize read counts per gene and number of independent Tn sites per gene
        # Generate pseudo-datasets with the same number of insertion sites and total reads mapping to those sites, randomly distributed across the genome
        counts.df <- data.frame(counts.norm)
        counts.df$Pos <- as.numeric(rownames(counts.df))
        numreads <- sum(counts.norm)/ctrl_reps
        numsites <- length(which(counts.norm > 0))/ctrl_reps
        
        #generates a new sites data frame and calculates the mean counts for each site in a new column. This column (containing the mean) is then used to sample from to generate the expected datasets.
        sites2 <- sites[2:(ctrl_reps + 1)]
        sites2$mean <- rowMeans(sites2) %>% round

        #For mariner transposon, define Possible_sites
        Possible_sites <- read_csv(paste0(TnSeq_folder, "/RefSeqs/Sau_USA300_FPR3757_TAsites.csv"), col_types = cols(...1 = col_skip())) #only need to do if mariner transposon
        colnames(Possible_sites) = c("sites")

        #compute expected dataset
        for (i in 1:num_expected) {
          expected <- data.frame(Pos = sample(Possible_sites$sites, numsites), Exp = sample(sites2$mean, numsites)) %>% arrange(Pos) 
                colnames(expected)[2] <- paste("Expected", i, sep = ".")
                counts.df <- merge(counts.df, expected, by = "Pos", all = T) %>% arrange(Pos)
                counts.df[is.na(counts.df)] <- 0
        }
        rownames(counts.df) <- counts.df$Pos
        counts.norm <- as.matrix(counts.df[,(2:length(counts.df))])
        
        write(paste("\n", "numreads: ", numreads, sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste("numsites: ", numsites, sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)

        # Initialize the lists of read counts per gene and number of independent Tn sites per gene
        controlreps <- 0
        expreps <- 0
        for (c in 1:length(counts.norm[1,])) {
                gff[,c + 9] <- rep(1,length(gff[,1]))
                if (controlreps < ctrl_reps) {
                        controlreps <- controlreps + 1
                        colnames(gff)[c + 9] <- paste(ctrl_pfx, controlreps, sep = ".")
                }
                else {
                        expreps <- expreps + 1
                        colnames(gff)[c + 9] <- paste("Expected", expreps, sep = ".")
                }
        }

        # Output gene boundaries and read counts per Tn site for Perl binning script
        boundariesfile <- paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, ".boundaries.tsv", sep = ""), sep = "")
        sitecountsfile <- paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, ".sitecounts.tsv", sep = ""), sep = "")
        write.table(gff[,c(4,5, 10:length(gff))], boundariesfile, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = F)
        write.table(counts.df, sitecountsfile, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = F)



Binning reads into genes
Teh TnGeneBin.pl script takes in the gene boundaries and read counts per site and outputs read counts per gene and number of sites per gene. The output files will be used for the DESeq2 analysis below.

myPath="data/TnSeq/"
cd $myPath
    
#input       
perl scripts/TnGeneBin.pl sites/sites_input/Sau_USA300_FPR3757_input_EssentialGenes_100.boundaries.tsv sites/sites_input/Sau_USA300_FPR3757_input_EssentialGenes_100.sitecounts.tsv  
#lac      
perl scripts/TnGeneBin.pl sites/sites_lac/Sau_USA300_FPR3757_lac_EssentialGenes_100.boundaries.tsv sites/sites_lac/Sau_USA300_FPR3757_lac_EssentialGenes_100.sitecounts.tsv 



Identifing essential genes with DESeq2
This code chunk reads in the output from the binning script, performs DESeq2 analysis to identify essential genes, and outputs the results. It also outputs summary statistics about the number of significant genes to a text file. It also needs to be runned separately for each sample type (input and lac) based on the mydata and ctrl_pfx variables defined above.

genecounts <- read.table(paste(boundariesfile, "out", sep = "."), header = T)[,-c(1,2)]
        genecounts2 <- read.table(paste(boundariesfile, "out", sep = "."), header = T)
        numsites <- read.table(paste(boundariesfile, "numsites.out", sep = "."), header = T)[,-c(1,2)]

        genes <- data.frame(id = rep("", length(gff[,1]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
        genes$id <- as.character(genes$id)
        for (i in 1:length(gff[,1])) {
                genes$id[i] <- strsplit(grep("locus_tag",strsplit(as.character(gff$att[i]),";")[[1]], value = T),"=")[[1]][2]
                genes$name[i] <- strsplit(grep("Name",strsplit(as.character(gff$att[i]),";")[[1]], value = T),"=")[[1]][2]

        }

        write.table(genecounts2, paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, ".genecounts2.tsv", sep = ""), sep = ""), quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)
        
        # Perform differential fitness analysis
        colnames(numsites) <- colnames(gff)[10:length(gff)] #change this number based on number of columns in gff
        numsitesout <- data.frame(numsites[,(1:ctrl_reps)])
        numsitesout[,ctrl_reps + 1] <- rowMeans(numsites[,-(1:ctrl_reps)])
        colnames(numsitesout)[ctrl_reps + 1] <- "Expected_numsites"
        colData <- data.frame(c(rep(ctrl_pfx, ctrl_reps), rep("Expected", num_expected)), condition = c(rep(ctrl_pfx, ctrl_reps),rep("Expected", num_expected)))
        numcountsout <- data.frame(genecounts2[,1:(ctrl_reps + 2)])
        numcountsout[,ctrl_reps + 3] <- rowMeans(genecounts2[,-(1:(ctrl_reps + 2))])
        colnames(numcountsout)[ctrl_reps + 3] <- "Expected_numreads"

        
        ###betaPrior=TRUE
        genescds_T <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = round(genecounts), colData = colData, design = ~ condition)
        #genescds_T <- newCountDataSet(round(genecounts), c(rep(ctrl_pfx, ctrl_reps), rep("Expected", num_expected)))
        #genescds_T$sizeFactor <- rep(1, length(genecounts[1,])) # This is manually set as 1 because we normalized by site above
        genescds_T <- estimateSizeFactors(genescds_T)
        genescds_T <- estimateDispersions(genescds_T) #can set fitType="local" if getting flag at this step for some samples
        genescds_T <- nbinomWaldTest(genescds_T, betaPrior = TRUE)
        res_T <- results(genescds_T, cooksCutoff = FALSE, contrast = c("condition", ctrl_pfx, "Expected"))
        print(head(res_T)) 
        #colnames(res_T)[4] <- paste(ctrl_pfx, "Mean", sep = "")
        #colnames(res_T)[3] <- "ExpectedMean"
        out_T <- cbind(res_T, genes$id, genes$name, numcountsout, numsitesout) # Uncomment if you have a kegg annotation
        #out_T <- cbind(res_T, genes[,2:3], numsitesout) %>% tbl_df # Uncomment if you do not have a kegg annotation
        colnames(out_T)[2] <- "log2FoldChange_TRUE"
        colnames(out_T)[3] <- "lfcSE_TRUE"
        colnames(out_T)[4] <- "stat_TRUE"
        colnames(out_T)[5] <- "pvalue_TRUE"
        colnames(out_T)[6] <- "padj_TRUE"
        colnames(out_T)[7] <- "id"

        #Count number of significant genes; can adjust pvalue and padj here based on output(s) that you are interested in
        write(paste("\n", "Analyses with betaPrior = TRUE (l2fc shrinkage):", sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste(paste("\n", "number of genes with pvalue <= 0.01 in TRUE:", sep = ""), sum(res_T$pvalue <= .01, na.rm = TRUE)), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste("number of genes with padj <= 0.01 in TRUE:", sum(res_T$padj <= .01, na.rm = TRUE)), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        
        # Perform bimodal clustering and essentiality calling and output results
        library(mclust)
        fit_T <- Mclust(out_T$log2FoldChange_TRUE, G = 1:2, modelNames = "V")
        summary(fit_T, parameters = TRUE)
        category_T <- rep("",length(out_T$id))
        for (i in 1:length(out_T$id)) {
          if (fit_T$classification[i] == 1 & out_T$log2FoldChange_TRUE[i] < 0) {
            category_T[i] <- "Reduced"
          }
          else {
            category_T[i] <- "Unchanged"
          }
        }
        
        density_T <- densityMclust(out_T$log2FoldChange_TRUE, G = 1:2, modelNames = "V")
        summary(density_T)
        pdf(paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "TRUE_histogram.pdf", sep = "_"), sep = ""), width = 10, height = 4)
        par(mfrow = c(1,2))
        plot(density_T, what = "density", data = out_T$log2FoldChange_TRUE, breaks = 100)
        plot(fit_T, what = "uncertainty")
        dev.off()
        
        #Count number of unchanged and reduced genes, l2fc means, and l2fc variances
        write(paste(paste("\n", "Mclust Unchanged TRUE:", sep = ""), sum(category_T == "Unchanged")), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste("Mclust Reduced TRUE:", sum(category_T == "Reduced")), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste(paste("\n","Mclust_reduced_mean_TRUE: ", sep = ""), fit_T$parameters$mean[1], sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste("Mclust_unchanged_mean_TRUE: ", fit_T$parameters$mean[2], sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste(paste("\n", "Mclust_reduced_variance_TRUE: ", sep = ""), fit_T$parameters$variance$sigmasq[1], sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste("Mclust_unchanged_variance_TRUE: ", fit_T$parameters$variance$sigmasq[2], sep = ""), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        
        fit_T$uncertainty[which(out_T$log2FoldChange_TRUE > 0)] <- 0
        print(head(category_T, 10))
        essentiality_T <- as.data.frame(cbind(category_T, fit_T$uncertainty))
        colnames(essentiality_T) <- c("Essentiality_TRUE", "Uncertainty_TRUE")
        out_T <- cbind(out_T, essentiality_T) 
        
        #Count number of significant genes with reduced Mclust; can adjust padj (or pvalue) and uncertaintly values here based on output(s) that you are interested in
        write(paste("\n", "Reduced and Uncertainty <=0.01 if TRUE:", sum(out_T$Essentiality_TRUE == "Reduced" & as.numeric(as.character(out_T$Uncertainty_TRUE)) <= 0.01)), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)
        write(paste("Reduced and Uncertainty <=0.01 and padj <=0.01 if TRUE:", sum(out_T$Essentiality_TRUE == "Reduced" & out_T$padj_TRUE <= .01 & as.numeric(as.character(out_T$Uncertainty_TRUE)) <= 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)), file = paste(mydata, "/", paste(out_pfx, "_stats.txt", sep = ""), sep = ""), append = TRUE)

plot_enrichment <- function(data, category, fdr_threshold = 0.05, top_n = 10, title = NULL) {
  
  df_plot <- data %>%
    filter(X.category == category,
           false.discovery.rate < fdr_threshold) %>%
    arrange(-enrichment.score) %>%
    head(top_n) %>%
    mutate(
      term.label = {
        if (category == "STRING clusters") {
          paste0(term.description, " (", term.ID, ")")
        } else {
          term.description
        }
      },
      term.label = str_replace_all(
        term.label,
        c("biosynthetic process" = "biosynthesis",
          "metabolic process" = "metabolism")
      ),
      term.label = str_wrap(term.label, width = 25),
      term.label = fct_reorder(term.label, enrichment.score)
    )
  
  plot <- ggplot(df_plot,aes(x = enrichment.score, y = term.label)) +
    
    geom_segment(aes(x = min(enrichment.score) * 0.92,   
                     xend = enrichment.score,

                     colour = false.discovery.rate),
                 linewidth = 1.2) +

  summarise(
    mean_OD600 = mean(OD600),
    sem_OD600 = sd(OD600) / sqrt(n()),  
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 


GC_plot_function <- function(data, media_filter, ymin = 0, ymax = 1.8) {
  # Filter data based on date and media type
  filtered_data <- data %>%
    filter(media %in% media_filter) %>%
    droplevels()
  
  # Create the growth curve plot
  growth_curve_plot <- ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = time, y = mean_OD600, color = strain, shape = vector)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        Parent  = "#5F05AF",
        "dat::Tn"  = "#2FD612",

      labels = c(

        "Δalr1" = "<b><span style='color:#03C0FF'>Δ  <i>alr1</i><span></b>"
      )
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c(
        None     = 16,  # filled circle
        EV     = 1,   # empty circle
        "PpepV dat"  = 17,  # filled triangle
        "Pdat dat"   = 2,   # empty triangle
        alr1  = 15   # filled square

        "Pdat dat" = "P<i><sub>dat</sub>dat</i>",
        alr1 = "P<i><sub>alr1</sub>alr1</i>"
      )
    ) +
    
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_OD600 - sem_OD600, ymax = mean_OD600 + sem_OD600), width = 0.2) +
    
    labs(title = paste(paste(media_filter)),
         x = "Time (hours)",
         y = "Mean OD<sub>600</sub> ± SEM") +
    
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(ymin, ymax), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(vjust = -10, hjust = 0.05, size = 14, face = "bold"),

      legend.title = element_markdown(size = 12),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),

      axis.title.y = element_markdown()
    ) +

  return(growth_curve_plot)
}

Stats and Supplemental Figures
The Area Under the Curve (AUC) was calculated for each growth curve to quantitatively compare the growth across different conditions. The AUC was computed using the trapezoidal rule from the pracma package.

# Calculate AUC for each growth curve using package pracma's trapz function, which performs numerical integration using the trapezoidal rule.
GC_AUC <- GC_OD600_20h %>%
  mutate(
    media = recode(media, "CDM19 - ala" = "CDM19Ala"),
    across(where(is.character), ~ str_replace_all(.x, " ", "")),
    across(where(is.factor), ~ factor(str_replace_all(as.character(.x), " ", "")))
  ) %>%
  group_by(label, media, strain, vector, date) %>%  
  summarise(AUC = trapz(time, OD600), .groups = "drop")

# Make a dataframe for each media condion for stats 
GC_AUC_CDM19Ala <- GC_AUC %>%
  filter(media == "CDM19Ala") %>%
  droplevels()

GC_AUC_TSB <- GC_AUC %>%
  filter(media == "TSB") %>%
  droplevels()

GC_AUC_CDM20 <- GC_AUC %>%
  filter(media == "CDM20") %>%
  droplevels()

We analyzed pairwise contrasts between Parent with the EV or no vector compared to all other strains. Also we look at all contrast within the strains dat::Tn and Δalr1. # Function to create a ggplot with jittered points, faceted by a variable, and customized aesthetics for fill and shape.
plot_comp_function <- function(data, ymin_exp, ymax_exp, title_x = " ", title_y = " ",
                          x_var, y_var, x_labels, fill_var, shape_var, facet_var, facet_labels,
                          fill_colors, shape_leves, facet_colors, fill_title, shape_title) {
  plot <- ggplot(data) +
    geom_jitter(
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = {{ y_var }}, fill = {{ fill_var }}, shape = {{ shape_var }}),
      size  = 4, stroke = 0.01, width = 0.2, color = "white") +
    
    facet_grid2(
      rows = NULL, cols = vars({{ facet_var }}),
      scales = "free_x", space = "free_x",
      strip = strip_themed(background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = facet_colors)),
      labeller = labeller(.cols = facet_labels)) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colors, name = fill_title) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = shape_leves, name = shape_title) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = x_labels) +
    
    guides(
      fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, color = "white", size = 3, stroke = 2)),
      shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "black", size = 3, stroke = 2))) +
    
    scale_y_log10(
      limits = c(10^ymin_exp, 10^ymax_exp),
      breaks = 10^(1:ymax_exp),
      labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))) +
    labs(x = title_x, y = title_y) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid    = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
      strip.text.x = element_markdown(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      text          = element_text(size = 16, color = "black"),
      axis.text.x   = element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
      axis.text.y   = element_text(color = "black")
    )
  
  return(plot)
}

                             x_var, y_var, x_labels, fill_var, shape_var, facet_var,
                             fill_colors, shape_leves, fill_title, shape_title) {
  
  annot <- formated_stats_results$main %>%
    filter(sign == "*") %>%
    mutate(sign = "")

  plot <- ggplot(data = formated_stats_results$input_data) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "#5F05AF", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_jitter(
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = {{ y_var }}, fill = {{ fill_var }}, shape = {{ shape_var }}),
      size  = 4, stroke = 0.01, width = 0.2, color = "white") +
    
    geom_point(data = formated_stats_results$predictions, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = predicted_mean), shape = 3, size = 1) +
    geom_errorbar(data = formated_stats_results$predictions, aes(x = {{ x_var }},
                                                                 y = predicted_mean,
                                                                 ymin = predicted_lower,
                                                                 ymax = predicted_upper),
                  width = .15) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colors, name = fill_title) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = shape_leves, name = shape_title) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = x_labels) +
    
    guides(
      fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, color = "white", size = 3, stroke = 2)),
      shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "black", size = 3, stroke = 2))) +
    
    scale_y_log10(
      breaks = 10^(ymin_exp:ymax_exp),
      labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))) +
    
    labs(x = title_x, y = title_y) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid    = element_blank(),
      text          = element_text(size = 16, color = "black"),
      axis.text.x   = element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
      axis.text.y   = element_text(color = "black")
    )

    plot <- plot +
      stat_pvalue_manual(annot, label = "sign", y.position = ymax_exp, 
                         step.increase = 0.04, tip.length = 0.01, bracket.shorten = 0.2, vjust = 0.6, bracket.size = 0.5) 
  }
  
  return(plot)
}

Chemical Complementation
Log-transformed CFU/HNO-ALI between groups were compared using a LMM to determine statistical significance with label (strain/media condition combined varaible) as a fixed effect and experimental date as a random effect (line was singular). We analyzed pairwise contrasts comparing all conditions to the unsupplemented parent strain (JE2) and all mutant (dat) conditions to the unsupplemented mutant strain. We then adjusted the p-values for multiple comparisons using the Holm method and created a sign annotation column to indicate which comparisons are statistically significant with p<0.05. Vertical brackets represent model-predicted mean values and confidence intervals (± 2 × SEM), back-transformed to the original response scale.

# Run the mixed model with emmeans contrasts
stats_results_Chem <- mixed_model_with_emmeans(
  input_data = CFUs_24h_Chem, response = "CFU_HNO", log_response = TRUE, adjust = "none",
  fixed_effects = c("label"), random_effects1 = "line", random_effects2 = "date"
)
stats_formated_Chem <- format_stats_results(stats_results_Chem, grouping_vars = c("condition", "plot_label", "parent_strain", "aa"))


# Filter the contrasts to only include those comparing to the unsupplemented JE2, dat and alr1 strains.
# Pvalues are adjusted using the Holm method only for the contrasts that are being kept and the significance annotation is added accordingly.
stats_formated_Chem$main = stats_formated_Chem$main %>%
  filter(condition1 == "JE2" | condition1 == "dat" | condition1 == "alr1") %>%
  filter(!(grepl("dat", condition1) & grepl("JE2|alr1", condition2))) %>%
  filter(!(grepl("alr1", condition1) & grepl("JE2|dat", condition2))) %>%
  mutate(
    p.value.adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "holm"),
    sign = case_when(
      p.value.adj < 0.05 & condition1 == "JE2" ~ "a",
      p.value.adj < 0.05 & condition1 == "dat" ~ "b",
      p.value.adj < 0.05 & condition1 == "alr1" ~ "c",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

# Save the stats results
saveRDS(stats_formated_Chem, file.path(outputs_folder, "stats_results_HNO_CFUs_Chemical.rds"))

# Function to create a ggplot with jittered points, emmeans predictions with error bars, and faceting. 
plot_Cps_function <- function(formated_stats_results, ymin_exp, ymax_exp, title_x = " ", title_y = " ",
                              x_var, y_var, x_labels, fill_var, shape_var, facet_var, facet_labels = NULL,
                              fill_colors, shape_leves, facet_colors, fill_title, shape_title) {
  plot <- ggplot(data = formated_stats_results$input_data) +
    geom_jitter(
      aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = {{ y_var }}, fill = {{ fill_var }}, shape = {{ shape_var }}),
      size  = 4, stroke = 0.01, width = 0.2, color = "white") +
    
    geom_point(data = formated_stats_results$predictions, aes(x = {{ x_var }}, y = predicted_mean), shape = 3, size = 1) +
    geom_errorbar(data = formated_stats_results$predictions, aes(x = {{ x_var }},
                                                                 y = predicted_mean,
                                                                 ymin = predicted_lower,
                                                                 ymax = predicted_upper),
                  width = .15) +
    
    facet_grid2(
      cols = vars({{ facet_var }}),
      scales = "free_x", space = "free_x",
      strip = strip_themed(background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = facet_colors)),
      labeller = if (!is.null(facet_labels)) labeller(.cols = facet_labels) else label_value
    ) +
    
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colors, name = fill_title) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = shape_leves, name = shape_title) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = x_labels) +
    
    guides(
      fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 22, color = "white", size = 3, stroke = 2)),
      shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "black", size = 3, stroke = 2))) +
    
    scale_y_log10(
      limits = c(10^ymin_exp, 10^ymax_exp),
      breaks = 10^(1:ymax_exp),
      labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))) +
    labs(x = title_x, y = title_y) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid    = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
      strip.text.x = element_markdown(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "white"),
      text          = element_text(size = 16, color = "black"),
      axis.text.x   = element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
      axis.text.y   = element_text(color = "black")
    )
  
  return(plot)
}

title: Linear Mixed Model Workflow
text:
mixed_model_with_emmeans()
This function fits a linear mixed-effects model and returns a structured list containing model summaries, ANOVA results, estimated marginal means, and post hoc contrasts.

Inputs

input_data: data frame containing the variables used in the model
response: name of the response variable as a character string
log_response: logical; if TRUE, the response is modeled as log(response)
fixed_effects: character vector of fixed-effect variable names; if more than one fixed effect is provided, interaction terms are included in the model
random_effects1: first random effect, typically a grouping factor such as line
random_effects2: optional second random effect, typically date, used to define an additional random grouping term (random_effects1:random_effects2) and as a fallback random effect if singularity is detected
adjust: p-value adjustment method passed to emmeans for multiple comparisons (for example "holm", "bonferroni", or "fdr")



What it does
The function programmatically constructs a model formula from the supplied arguments. If log_response = TRUE, the response variable is log-transformed before fitting. For example:

one fixed effect: log(response) ~ factor1 + (1|line)
two fixed effects: log(response) ~ factor1 * factor2 + (1|line) + (1|line:date)

The function then:

fits the model with lmer() from the lme4 (Bates et al., 2015) package
checks model singularity with isSingular()
if singularity is detected and random_effects2 is provided, simplifies the random-effects structure and refits the model using the same fixed-effects formula but with (1|random_effects2) as the random effect
extracts summaries of the random and fixed effects
computes ANOVA statistics using the lmerTest (Kuznetsova et al., 2017) package, which provides F-tests and p-values using the default Satterthwaite approximation for denominator degrees of freedom
computes estimated marginal means and pairwise contrasts for the specified fixed effects and, when applicable, interaction contrasts, using the emmeans (Lenth and Piaskowski, 2025) package with p-values adjusted by the specified method
returns estimated marginal mean predictions and approximate confidence bounds; if the response variable was log-transformed, these predictions are back-transformed to the original response scale for interpretability



Outputs
The returned object is a list containing:

input_data: the input data with a combined condition column added for downstream matching and plotting
model_formula: the fitted model formula
anova: ANOVA table for the fitted model
random_effects: variance components extracted from the random-effects structure
fixed_effects: fixed-effect coefficient table from summary(model)
emmeans_formula: formula used to generate estimated marginal means
emmeans_contrasts: pairwise contrasts for main effects and, when applicable, interactions
emmeans_predictions: estimated marginal means with back-transformed predictions and confidence bounds



Function definition
function (input_data, response, log_response, fixed_effects, 
    random_effects1 = NULL, random_effects2 = NULL, adjust) 
{
    fixed_formula <- paste(fixed_effects, collapse = " * ")
    rand1 <- if (!is.null(random_effects1)) 
        paste0("(1|", random_effects1, ")")
    else NULL
    rand2 <- if (!is.null(random_effects2)) 
        paste0("(1|", random_effects1, ":", random_effects2, 
            ")")
    else NULL
    random_formula <- paste(na.omit(c(rand1, rand2)), collapse = " + ")
    response_part <- if (log_response) {
        paste0("log(", response, ")")
    }
    else {
        response
    }
    formula_str <- paste(response_part, "~", fixed_formula, "+", 
        random_formula)
    model_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)
    model <- lmer(model_formula, data = input_data)
    singular <- isSingular(model)
    random_effects_df <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model)) %>% mutate(proportion = round(100 * 
        (vcov/sum(vcov)), 2)) %>% mutate(singular = singular)
    if (singular && !is.null(random_effects2)) {
        fallback_formula_str <- paste(response_part, "~", fixed_formula, 
            "+", paste0("(1|", random_effects2, ")"))
        model_formula <- as.formula(fallback_formula_str)
        model <- lmer(model_formula, data = input_data)
    }
    anova_tbl <- anova(model)
    effect_names <- rownames(anova_tbl)
    fixed_effects_df <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients) %>% 
        rownames_to_column(var = "term")
    emmeans_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", fixed_formula))
    emmeans_model <- emmeans(model, emmeans_formula)
    emmeans_contrasts <- lapply(fixed_effects, function(effect) {
        summary(pairs(emmeans_model, simple = effect, adjust = adjust))
    })
    names(emmeans_contrasts) <- fixed_effects
    if (length(fixed_effects) > 1) {
        emmeans_contrasts[["interaction"]] <- summary(contrast(emmeans_model, 
            interaction = rep("pairwise", length(fixed_effects)), 
            by = NULL), adjust = adjust)
    }
    emmeans_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans_model)
    emmeans_df <- emmeans_df %>% mutate(predicted_mean = if (log_response) 
        exp(emmean)
    else emmean, predicted_lower = if (log_response) 
        exp(emmean - 2 * SE)
    else emmean - 2 * SE, predicted_upper = if (log_response) 
        exp(emmean + 2 * SE)
    else emmean + 2 * SE, condition = paste(!!!syms(fixed_effects), 
        sep = ".")) %>% filter(!is.na(emmean)) %>% droplevels()
    input_data <- input_data %>% mutate(condition = paste(!!!syms(fixed_effects), 
        sep = "."))
    return(list(input_data = input_data, model_formula = model_formula, 
        anova = anova_tbl, random_effects = random_effects_df, 
        fixed_effects = fixed_effects_df, emmeans_formula = emmeans_formula, 
        emmeans_contrasts = emmeans_contrasts, emmeans_predictions = emmeans_df))
}

text:
format_stats_results()
This function takes the output of mixed_model_with_emmeans() and reformats it into tidy tables that are easier to join, filter, annotate, and plot.

Inputs

stats_results: the list returned by mixed_model_with_emmeans()
grouping_vars: variables used to summarize the original observed data alongside model predictions. The default is condition, a combined variable created in mixed_model_with_emmeans(), but additional variables from the original data can be included when needed for downstream plotting or annotation.
p.value_threshold: threshold used to create a simple significance label column (sign); the default is 0.05



What it does
This function:

summarizes the original observed data by group and calculates the mean and standard error for each group, which can be used for plotting alongside model predictions
joins those summaries to the emmeans predictions
matches each contrast to its corresponding predicted means, allowing calculation of fold changes (FC) and log2 fold changes (log2FC) between contrast groups
returns a clean structure for downstream visualization and reporting, including columns named group1 and group2 that can be used to annotate significant differences in plots, as well as a simple significance label (sign) based on the specified p-value threshold



Outputs
The returned object is a list containing:

input_data: the original input data with a combined condition column
predictions: estimated marginal means joined with observed summary statistics
main: formatted main-effect contrasts with columns for group1, group2, FC, log2FC, and sign
interaction: formatted interaction contrasts, if present
anova: passed through from mixed_model_with_emmeans()
random_effects: passed through from mixed_model_with_emmeans()
fixed_effects: passed through from mixed_model_with_emmeans()



Function definition
function (stats_results, grouping_vars = c("condition"), p.value_threshold = 0.05) 
{
    input_data <- stats_results$input_data
    predictions <- stats_results$emmeans_predictions
    contrasts <- stats_results$emmeans_contrasts
    response <- stats_results$model_formula[[2]]
    anova <- stats_results$anova
    random_effects <- stats_results$random_effects
    fixed_effects <- stats_results$fixed_effects
    if (is.call(response) && identical(response[[1]], as.name("log"))) {
        response <- response[[2]]
    }
    input_summary <- input_data %>% group_by(across(all_of(grouping_vars))) %>% 
        summarise(n = n(), mean = mean({
            {
                response
            }
        }), sd = sd({
            {
                response
            }
        }), se = sd/sqrt(n), .groups = "drop")
    predictions <- predictions %>% left_join(input_summary, by = "condition")
    effect_names <- names(contrasts)
    main_effects <- setdiff(effect_names, "interaction")
    has_interaction <- "interaction" %in% effect_names
    anova_effect_names <- rownames(stats_results$anova)
    anova_pvalues <- stats_results$anova$`Pr(>F)`
    names(anova_pvalues) <- anova_effect_names
    process_main_effect <- function(name) {
        contr <- contrasts[[name]]
        contr$effect_name <- name
        contr$p.value.anova <- anova_pvalues[name]
        contr <- contr %>% mutate(contrast = str_replace_all(contrast, 
            "\\s+", ""))
        contr <- contr %>% separate(contrast, into = c("condition1", 
            "condition2"), sep = "-", remove = FALSE, fill = "right")
        other_effect <- setdiff(main_effects, name)
        if (length(other_effect) == 1 && other_effect %in% names(contr)) {
            if (name == main_effects[1]) {
                contr <- contr %>% mutate(condition1 = paste(condition1, 
                  .data[[other_effect]], sep = "."), condition2 = paste(condition2, 
                  .data[[other_effect]], sep = "."))
            }
            else {
                contr <- contr %>% mutate(condition1 = paste(.data[[other_effect]], 
                  condition1, sep = "."), condition2 = paste(.data[[other_effect]], 
                  condition2, sep = "."))
            }
        }
        contr
    }
    main_contrasts <- lapply(main_effects, process_main_effect)
    main_contrasts_tbl <- bind_rows(main_contrasts) %>% select(effect_name, 
        p.value.anova, contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value, 
        everything())
    main_contrasts_tbl <- main_contrasts_tbl %>% left_join(dplyr::select(predictions, 
        condition, predicted_mean), by = join_by(condition1 == 
        condition)) %>% left_join(dplyr::select(predictions, 
        condition, predicted_mean), by = join_by(condition2 == 
        condition), suffix = c(".1", ".2")) %>% mutate(FC = predicted_mean.1/predicted_mean.2, 
        log2FC = log2(FC), sign = case_when(p.value < p.value_threshold ~ 
            "*", TRUE ~ ""))
    conditions_label_col = grouping_vars[1]
    main_contrasts_tbl$group1 <- predictions[[conditions_label_col]][match(main_contrasts_tbl$condition1, 
        predictions$condition)]
    main_contrasts_tbl$group2 <- predictions[[conditions_label_col]][match(main_contrasts_tbl$condition2, 
        predictions$condition)]
    interaction_tbl <- NULL
    if (has_interaction) {
        inter_contr <- contrasts$interaction
        inter_contr$effect_name <- "interaction"
        interaction_anova_name <- names(anova_pvalues)[grepl(":", 
            names(anova_pvalues))]
        inter_contr$p.value.anova <- anova_pvalues[interaction_anova_name]
        interaction_tbl <- inter_contr %>% select(effect_name, 
            p.value.anova, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value, 
            everything()) %>% mutate(sign = case_when(p.value < 
            p.value_threshold ~ "*", TRUE ~ ""))
    }
    return(list(input_data = input_data, predictions = predictions, 
        main = main_contrasts_tbl, interaction = interaction_tbl, 
        anova = anova, random_effects = random_effects, fixed_effects = fixed_effects))
}
